plant.description: A small electric heater with a temperature sensor. Input u in [0,1] is heater power; the device loses heat to the room on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a normalized temperature reading (0 = 15 °C, 1 = 75 °C).

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces uncertainty in response direction, lag, and approximate gain magnitude, which are required to choose any stabilizing controller gain and steady-state feedforward.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain heater hypothesis is right, y will rise monotonically from ~0.24 after a short lag toward ~0.35-0.45, slope positive but flattening by end, with small noise and no fall.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces uncertainty in u=0 decay, ambient level, cooling lag/time-constant and noise, which are required to estimate steady-state gain and choose feedforward plus integral action.
experiments.expected_observation: If cooling/decay hypothesis is right, y will fall monotonically from ~0.435 toward ~0.20-0.25 with no initial rise, fast negative slope at first then flattening toward zero slope by end, with jitter ~0.01-0.02 but no sustained rise.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces uncertainty in steady-state gain linearity and the input needed to hold 0.5 plus time-constant, which are required to choose feedforward and feedback gains.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain with tau~170-200s is right, y will stay ~0.15 for ~20-30s then rise monotonically toward ~0.50-0.55 by end, slope still positive ~0.0005-0.001 but flattening, with jitter ~0.02-0.03 and no sustained fall.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces uncertainty in steady-state gain and the feedforward input needed to hold 0.5 plus time-constant from the falling trajectory, which are required to choose feedforward and PI gains.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain first-order with tau ~150-200s and y_ss(0.35)~0.48-0.55 is right, y will hold ~0.54 for ~20-30s lag then drift down slowly toward ~0.50-0.53 by end, slope small negative flattening, jitter ~0.02 with no sustained rise.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces uncertainty in steady-state gain and the feedforward input needed to hold 0.5 and falling time-constant, which are required to choose feedforward and PI gains.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain first-order with lag ~20-30s and tau ~150-200s and y_ss(0.35) ~0.46-0.53 is right, y will hold ~0.55-0.59 for ~20-30s then drift slowly down toward ~0.50-0.55 by end with small negative slope flattening, jitter ~0.02-0.03 and no sustained rise above 0.62.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces uncertainty in falling time-constant and the steady-state input needed to hold 0.5 by approaching the same 0.3 level from above, which is required to choose feedforward and PI gains and to test linearity symmetry.
experiments.expected_observation: If first-order positive-gain with lag ~20-30s, tau ~150-220s and y_ss(0.3)~0.46-0.52 is right, y will dwell ~0.59-0.62 for ~20-30s then fall monotonically toward ~0.54-0.57 by end, end slope still negative ~-0.0003 to -0.0008, jitter ~0.02 with no sustained rise above 0.64.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces uncertainty in falling time-constant near 0.5 and the feedforward input needed to hold target, which determines controller steady-state and anti-overshoot tuning.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain first-order with lag 20-30s, tau ~180-250s and y_ss(0.3)~0.49-0.52 is right, y will dwell ~0.60-0.64 for ~20-30s then fall monotonically toward ~0.57-0.59 by end, end slope small negative ~-0.0005 to -0.001 and flattening, jitter ~0.02 with no sustained rise above 0.66.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces uncertainty in falling time-constant near 0.5-0.6 and the feedforward input needed to hold 0.5, which determines controller steady-state and anti-overshoot tuning.
experiments.expected_observation: If first-order positive-gain with lag 20-30s, tau 150-250s and y_ss(0.32)~0.48-0.54 is right, y will dwell near 0.60 for ~20-30s then fall monotonically to ~0.55-0.57 by end, end slope small negative ~-0.0004 to -0.001 and flattening, jitter ~0.02 with no sustained rise above 0.63.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Distinguishes weaker actuator vs faster outflow vs longer delay vs sensor offset by measuring delay from last command change and u=0 fall rate versus E2, which determines whether to raise feedforward gain, add loss compensation, retune for slower dynamics, or correct for offset.
experiments.expected_observation: If weaker-actuator-with-unchanged-cooling is right, y will keep responding to the prior ~0.47 command for ~20-30s holding ~0.38-0.40, then fall monotonically following the E2 trajectory toward ~0.14-0.18 by end with flattening slope and ~0.02 jitter; a clearly faster fall to <0.12 or much slower start would favor faster-outflow or longer-delay instead.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Reduces uncertainty in post-change heating gain and delay from low ambient, discriminating weaker actuator vs larger loss vs slower dynamics vs sensor shift, which determines required feedforward increase vs loss compensation vs retuning vs offset correction.
experiments.expected_observation: If C1 weaker-actuator with unchanged cooling/delay-shortened is right, y will hold ~0.14 for <10s (no 20-30s dwell) then rise monotonically toward only ~0.35-0.42 by end, slope still positive but flattening, jitter ~0.01-0.02; E3 same step reached 0.524 and still rising, so a clearly lower end-level with similar time-shape favors weaker gain, a much faster flattening below 0.35 favors larger loss, a long >30s flat then very slow rise favors C3, and an E3-like shape shifted down by constant favors sensor offset.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Delay from last command change and u=0 cooling tau versus E2, discriminating weaker actuator (unchanged delay/tau) from faster outflow (faster fall) vs slower response (longer delay/slower fall), which determines whether to raise feedforward gain, add loss compensation, or retune for slower dynamics.
experiments.expected_observation: If C1 weaker-actuator with unchanged delay/tau is right, y will keep responding to prior 0.5 for ~15-30s rising to ~0.31-0.33, then fall monotonically toward ~0.13-0.15 following E9/E2 shape with tau ~150-180s and flattening slope, jitter ~0.01-0.02; immediate fall with no rise would imply shortened delay, fall to <0.12 or clearly faster than E2 would favor larger loss, >30s flat then very slow fall would favor slower dynamics.

ledger.statement: Increasing u increases steady-state y (positive gain heater).

Baseline step response has lag ~15-35s plus dominant time-constant ~150-250s; E1 slope +0.0022 after 300s unsettled, E3 rise over 220s with ~20s lag, E7 dwell ~30s then fall, E10 similar ~20s onset, E11 hold ~16-24s then fall.
There is no large dead zone: u=0.3 produces clear rise in E1 and fall in E7, u=0.5 rises promptly after lag in E3 and E10, u=0 falls in E2/E9/E11.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward ambient ~0.12-0.16; E2 ended 0.148-0.15, E9 ended 0.138-0.141, E11 ended 0.136 with same shape.
Baseline steady-state y(u) is approximately linear with slope K~1.0-1.2 and intercept ~0.12-0.16.
Baseline steady-state input to hold y=0.5 is 0.30-0.35, likely ~0.32-0.33.
Baseline sensor jitter is ~0.02-0.04 with occasional 0.03-0.05 swings; E9/E10/E11 show similar jitter, E3 end to E7 start jump ~0.13 and E10 end to E11 start ~0.04 remain far above jitter.
The +0.12-0.13 discontinuity between E3 end and E7 start and +0.04 between E10 end and E11 start implies continued heating at u=0.5 between experiments, an external disturbance, or logging offset.

Change is weaker actuator: same u gives smaller rise (~44% in E10 0.163 vs E3 0.374), but u=0 cooling rate/ambient and delay unchanged, so u=0 fall matches E2 scaled and same u holds lower steady state; monitoring shows u 0.354->0.468 while y 0.48->0.38 falling.
Change is faster outflow / larger heat loss: u=0 fall is faster than E2 and same u holds lower level, while actuator gain is unchanged.
Change is slower dynamics with unchanged steady-state gain: pure delay >30s or tau much larger than 250s, so E10 low level is transient still rising toward ~0.6.
Change is sensor shift: true thermal dynamics unchanged but reading has offset or lower gain, so u=0 reading would settle below 0.12-0.16 or noise differs.
